title: Better World Models Can Lead to Better Post-Training Performance
abstract: arXiv:2512.03400v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: We study how explicit world-modeling objectives affect the internal representations and downstream capability of Transformers, using Rubik's Cubes as our training domain. We ask: (1) how does explicitly pretraining a world model affect a model's latent representations, (2) how does world-model quality affect post-training performance, and (3) how should a finite data budget be split between pretraining and task-specific fine-tuning? We compare standard action-prediction fine-tuning with two strategies that add explicit state-prediction supervision: state pretraining followed by fine-tuning, and joint action and state training. We measure task accuracy after Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). translated_title: 更好的世界模型能带来更好的后训练性能
translated_abstract: 我们研究了显式世界建模目标如何影响 Transformer 的内部表征与下游能力，并以魔方作为训练领域。我们探讨三个问题：(1) 显式预训练世界模型会如何影响模型的潜在表征；(2) 世界模型的质量如何影响后训练性能；(3) 在有限的数据预算下，应如何在预训练与任务特定微调之间进行分配？我们将标准的动作预测微调与两种引入显式状态预测监督的策略进行比较：先进行状态预训练再微调，以及动作与状态的联合训练。我们在群体相对策略优化（GRPO）之后测量任务准确率。我们进一步发现，显式世界建模能带来更好的表征——体现在更高的探测准确率与更强的模型可控性上——并且更好的表征能从 GRPO 中获得更大的收益，尤其是在更难的魔方状态上。
tldr: 该论文以魔方为实验领域，发现为 Transformer 引入显式世界建模（状态预测）监督能改善其内部表征，而更好的表征能在 GRPO 后训练中带来更大的性能提升，尤其是在更难的魔方状态上。
en_tdlr: Using Rubik's Cubes as a testbed, this paper shows that adding explicit world-modeling (state-prediction) supervision to Transformers yields better latent representations, which in turn lead to larger post-training (GRPO) performance gains, especially on harder cube states.
